allObjections.title: Telemetry-only dims create shadow metrics
allObjections.detail: §10.1 dims 6-7 emit telemetry that operators will inevitably use for decisions despite being excluded from §7.6 score. This creates a shadow metric system where content_quality_finding and accessibility_finding accumulate in dashboards but have no canonical interpretation or threshold.

allObjections.title: Purpose field atomicity gap
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B-v2 adds product_purpose as optional free-form text on product_registry but provides no atomic-write guarantee. Unlike the 6 canonical blocks protected by CA-14-D-Q1, this field could be partially written or corrupted without triggering rollback.

allObjections.title: Drift tier thresholds undefined
allObjections.detail: CA-15-C-v2-Q3 mentions 20%/50% token-change thresholds in options but the proposal text never defines how PURPOSE_DRIFT_MINOR/MAJOR/CRITICAL are calculated. Without concrete thresholds, operators cannot predict when drift notifications will trigger.

allObjections.title: CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md creates circular dependency
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D-v2 delegates CEO re-sign triggers to docs/governance/CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md which doesn't exist yet. This file must list which files trigger re-sign, but editing CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md itself could require re-sign, creating an infinite regress.

allObjections.title: Admin-only opt-in complexity
allObjections.detail: The proposal introduces an admin-only opt-in mechanism for dimensions 6 and 7 in §10.1, which could complicate the configuration process and limit flexibility for operators who may need these dimensions without admin intervention.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only findings risk
allObjections.detail: By making content_quality and accessibility findings telemetry-only, the proposal risks underemphasizing these important aspects, potentially allowing products with poor content quality or accessibility to pass audits without sufficient scrutiny.

allObjections.title: Purpose information ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The removal of the `purpose_record` block and reliance on an optional free-form `product_purpose` field could lead to inconsistencies in how purpose information is captured and used, as there is no structured schema or validation.

allObjections.title: Lack of Validation
allObjections.detail: The proposal does not provide sufficient validation for the `product_purpose` field, which could lead to inconsistent or misleading data. Specifically, §7.5 does not define any validation rules for this field.

allObjections.title: Inconsistent Scoring
allObjections.detail: The §7.6 score formula does not account for content quality and accessibility findings, which could result in an incomplete or inaccurate assessment of the product's quality. This is evident in the §7.6 score formula, which only considers crit, high, med, and low findings.

allObjections.title: Overreliance on Admin Opt-in
allObjections.detail: The proposal relies heavily on admin opt-in for dims 6 and 7, which may not be sufficient to ensure that these dimensions are properly considered. This is a concern because the admin opt-in mechanism is not clearly defined in §10.1.

allObjections.title: Complexity of admin-opt-in mechanism
allObjections.detail: The admin-opt-in mechanism for extending the quality dimensions in §10.1 introduces unnecessary complexity. It requires admin intervention for enabling dimensions that could be beneficial for all products. This might lead to inconsistent quality audits across different products.

allObjections.title: Lack of LLM-judged purpose-alignment check
allObjections.detail: Removing the LLM-judged purpose-alignment check from the Purpose-Driven Optimization loop exit criteria may result in optimizations that do not align with the product's purpose. This could lead to suboptimal outcomes that do not meet the intended goals of the product.

allObjections.title: Potential misuse of free-form product_purpose field
allObjections.detail: The optional free-form `product_purpose` field in the ProductSSOT may lead to inconsistent and unvalidated purpose statements. Without proper validation, this field could be misused or left empty, defeating the purpose of having a product_purpose field in the first place.

allObjections.title: Risk of false positives in drift annotation
allObjections.detail: The tiered drift annotation system may lead to false positives, especially in the major and critical tiers. This could result in unnecessary operator interventions and potential freezes on fixes, disrupting the continuous improvement process.

allObjections.title: Admin-opt-in complexity
allObjections.detail: The admin-opt-in mechanism for dimensions 6 and 7 introduces unnecessary complexity and potential for misconfiguration.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only findings
allObjections.detail: Content quality and accessibility findings being telemetry-only may lead to these issues being overlooked by operators.

allObjections.title: Optional purpose field
allObjections.detail: The optional nature of the `product_purpose` field may result in inconsistent or missing purpose statements across products.

allObjections.title: Admin-only opt-in complexity
allObjections.detail: The admin-only opt-in for dims 6 & 7 in §10.1 adds complexity without a clear benefit. It introduces a configuration flag that needs to be managed and understood, potentially leading to confusion and inconsistent application of quality checks across products.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only findings risk neglect
allObjections.detail: Treating content_quality and accessibility findings as telemetry-only in §7.6 risks neglecting these important aspects of product quality. If these findings don't directly impact the score, they may be deprioritized or ignored, leading to a decline in overall product quality.

allObjections.title: Optional product_purpose ambiguity
allObjections.detail: The optional free-form `product_purpose` field in `product_registry` lacks structure and validation, making it difficult to use effectively. The absence of a schema and the reliance on operator-supplied text can lead to inconsistent and unreliable purpose statements.

allObjections.title: Tiered drift annotation complexity
allObjections.detail: The tiered drift annotation (minor/major/critical) adds unnecessary complexity to the system. The distinctions between the tiers and their corresponding actions may not be clear, leading to inconsistent application and potential confusion for operators.

allObjections.title: Advisory SSOT-Conformance Gate weakness
allObjections.detail: Making the §27 SSOT-Conformance Gate advisory-only weakens its effectiveness. Without a hard blocking gate, operators may choose to ignore conformance issues, leading to a decline in the overall quality and reliability of the system.

allObjections.title: §10.1 dimension overlap
allObjections.detail: The proposed Content Quality dimension overlaps with existing UI/UX scoring criteria without clear differentiation boundaries. This creates ambiguity in §10.1 audit reports where the same visual/text issues could be counted under both dimensions, leading to inconsistent weighting and potential double-reporting.

allObjections.title: Optional purpose field risk
allObjections.detail: The free-form product_purpose field lacks validation or structured schema, making it vulnerable to misuse and misinterpretation. Without mandatory format rules or automated consistency checks, operators could enter contradictory, outdated, or overly vague purpose statements that undermine drift detection mechanisms.

allObjections.title: Drift thresholds arbitrary
allObjections.detail: The 20%/50% token-change thresholds for minor/major/critical drift annotations lack empirical justification. These arbitrary cutoffs may misclassify significant semantic changes as minor if token delta is low, or flag harmless refactors as critical drift, creating noise in governance records.

allObjections.title: Conformance scope maintenance
allObjections.detail: Maintaining CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md as the trigger for CEO re-sign introduces documentation drift risk. The file requires manual updates for every relevant CA, creating a brittle dependency where missed updates could invalidate sign-offs or allow non-conforming changes to bypass scrutiny.

allObjections.title: Telemetry-only weakens enforcement
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A-v2-Q2 moves content_quality and accessibility findings out of §7.6 entirely and into dashboard-only telemetry. That means a product can repeatedly fail copy/accessibility checks while still posting a clean readiness score, which undermines the existing score as an operator-facing risk signal.

allObjections.title: Admin-opt-in hides regressions
allObjections.detail: In CA-15-A-v2-Q3, dims 6 and 7 are off by default and admin-only, but the proposal still exposes them as quality dimensions in §10.1. This creates a split-brain audit where most products never see these checks in the acceptance path, so regressions can ship unless someone remembers to enable the knob product-by-product.

allObjections.title: Purpose field is too underspecified
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B-v2 replaces the canonical `purpose_record` with an optional free-form `product_purpose` string on `product_registry`, but provides no schema, length limit, provenance, or write-atomicity rule beyond a general note. That invites stale, contradictory, or promotional purpose text to become de facto canonical state without any structured validation or lifecycle management.

allObjections.title: Drift annotations may mask deadlocks
allObjections.detail: CA-15-C-v2-Q3 converts PURPOSE_DRIFT into minor/major/critical annotations, but the proposal does not specify a deterministic transition rule from annotation to operator disposition or freeze. In practice, major drift can accumulate across runs while still allowing the loop to continue, making the issue visible but not actionable.

allObjections.title: Scoped re-sign is gameable
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D-v2-Q2 limits CEO re-sign invalidation to files listed in `docs/governance/CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md`. Because that scope file is itself editable documentation, the system can drift into a state where consequential governance changes are made adjacent to, but not inside, the tracked scope and therefore avoid re-sign requirements.

allObjections.title: Overly Complex §10.1 Extension
allObjections.detail: The proposal extends §10.1 with two new dimensions (Content Quality and Accessibility) but introduces complexity with admin-opt-in and telemetry-only findings. This may lead to inconsistent application and confusion among operators.

allObjections.title: Lack of Validation for `product_purpose`
allObjections.detail: The optional `product_purpose` field is introduced without a strict schema or validation rules, potentially leading to inconsistent or malformed data entry.

allObjections.title: Removal of `purpose_record` Block
allObjections.detail: Removing `purpose_record` as a canonical block may reduce the system's ability to track and validate product purpose, potentially impacting Purpose-Driven Optimization.

allObjections.title: §10.1 dim extension overlap unresolved
allObjections.detail: CA-15-A v2 extends the existing §10.1 5-dim engine (UI/UX, API, Logic, Business Value, Security Posture) with optional dims 6/7 but provides no explicit conflict-resolution rule for UI/UX vs Content Quality double-counting, despite citing Slot 1 and Slot 10 objections from v1.

allObjections.title: product_purpose field lacks validation
allObjections.detail: CA-15-B v2 adds optional free-form product_purpose to product_registry without required-field rules, atomic-write enforcement, or schema validation, directly contradicting the §7.5 atomic ProductSSOT update invariant and CA-14-D-Q1 guarantees.

allObjections.title: §27 gate advisory weakens §25 rules
allObjections.detail: CA-15-D v2 converts the §27 SSOT-Conformance Gate to advisory-only telemetry via governance_record_entry, eroding the Locked Rules §25 requirement that every CA promotion must maintain strict conformance without operator bypass.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: The advisory-only §27 gate allows non-conformant deployments to proceed with just a telemetry emission, making the entire conformance testing infrastructure optional theater that operators will learn to ignore.
adversarial.precedent: Kubernetes deprecated PodSecurityPolicy in favor of Pod Security Standards partly because the advisory-only mode created confusion about which violations actually mattered, leading to production clusters with hundreds of ignored warnings.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This proposal fragments quality assessment across three incompatible surfaces: canonical §10.1 5-dim scoring that blocks pipelines, optional dims 6-7 that emit ignorable telemetry, and a purpose field with no validation or integration. The structural rewrite replaces v1's coherent (if flawed) vision with a collection of half-measures that increase complexity without improving outcomes. Defer until a unified quality framework emerges.

CA-15-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — leave §10.1 at 5 dims; content quality + accessibility live in tooling only.
CA-15-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Adding optional dims that don't affect pipeline outcomes creates confusion about what 'quality' means in FlowAI; better to keep quality assessment unified.

CA-15-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify with stricter wording — explicit invariant: "§7.6 formula NEVER absorbs content_quality_finding / accessibility_finding counts."
CA-15-A-v2-Q2.rationale: If these findings truly stay telemetry-only, the invariant must be explicit to prevent future scope creep.

CA-15-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Defer — opt-in semantics belong in operator-config doc, not canonical §10.1.
CA-15-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Admin-only flags for quality dimensions are operational choices that shouldn't be hardcoded in canonical governance specs.

CA-15-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject the optional field too — no purpose information lives in ProductSSOT.
CA-15-B-v2-Q1.rationale: An unvalidated free-form text field adds no value over external documentation and creates false expectations about purpose-driven features.

CA-15-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Given the field exists, limiting to operator-supplied purpose avoids the hallucination risks of inferred modes.

CA-15-B-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (placeholder detection in tooling, not canonical).
CA-15-B-v2-Q3.rationale: Placeholder detection is a development-time concern that belongs in linting tools, not runtime governance.

CA-15-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (5 numeric exits; no LLM check).
CA-15-C-v2-Q1.rationale: Removing LLM-judged purpose alignment eliminates a major source of non-determinism in the optimization loop.

CA-15-C-v2-Q2.rationale: Without LLM purpose scoring, the 0.7 threshold has no meaning and should be removed.

CA-15-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Reject — drift should never block; reduce to single advisory annotation.
CA-15-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Three drift tiers with undefined thresholds and different escalation paths adds complexity without clear operator benefit.

CA-15-D-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — §27 should stay a hard blocking gate as v1 proposed.
CA-15-D-v2-Q1.rationale: Making conformance advisory-only defeats the purpose of having conformance tests; violations should block deployment.

CA-15-D-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify with broader scope — any CA editing src/lib/governance/ also triggers.
CA-15-D-v2-Q2.rationale: Scoping re-sign triggers to a not-yet-existing file creates implementation uncertainty; src/lib/governance/ is a concrete scope.

CA-15-B-v2-Q3.rationale: Keeps the system clean while allowing for necessary checks.

CA-15-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (5 numeric exits; no LLM check).
CA-15-C-v2-Q1.rationale: Removes reliance on potentially unreliable LLM judgments.

CA-15-C-v2-Q2.rationale: Simplifies the exit criteria and removes arbitrary thresholds.

CA-15-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minor: log; major: operator dispose; critical: freeze fixes + Panel notify).

perReviewer.overallNotes: The proposal, while well-intentioned, introduces several points of complexity and potential oversight that may degrade the overall system effectiveness.

objections.title: Admin-only opt-in complexity
objections.detail: The admin-only opt-in for dims 6 & 7 in §10.1 adds complexity without a clear benefit. It introduces a configuration flag that needs to be managed and understood, potentially leading to confusion and inconsistent application of quality checks across products.

objections.title: Telemetry-only findings risk neglect
objections.detail: Treating content_quality and accessibility findings as telemetry-only in §7.6 risks neglecting these important aspects of product quality. If these findings don't directly impact the score, they may be deprioritized or ignored, leading to a decline in overall product quality.

objections.title: Optional product_purpose ambiguity
objections.detail: The optional free-form `product_purpose` field in `product_registry` lacks structure and validation, making it difficult to use effectively. The absence of a schema and the reliance on operator-supplied text can lead to inconsistent and unreliable purpose statements.

objections.title: Tiered drift annotation complexity
objections.detail: The tiered drift annotation (minor/major/critical) adds unnecessary complexity to the system. The distinctions between the tiers and their corresponding actions may not be clear, leading to inconsistent application and potential confusion for operators.

objections.title: Advisory SSOT-Conformance Gate weakness
objections.detail: Making the §27 SSOT-Conformance Gate advisory-only weakens its effectiveness. Without a hard blocking gate, operators may choose to ignore conformance issues, leading to a decline in the overall quality and reliability of the system.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: By making the SSOT-Conformance Gate advisory-only, operators might ignore critical conformance issues, leading to a deployment of a product that violates key SSOT principles, ultimately degrading the overall system's reliability and maintainability compared to the current state where such violations would be caught and blocked.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: This proposal, while attempting to address previous concerns, introduces new complexities and weakens critical aspects of the system. The admin-only opt-in, telemetry-only findings, optional purpose field, tiered drift annotation, and advisory conformance gate collectively create a system that is more difficult to manage, less reliable, and potentially less effective than the status quo. Deferring the proposal would allow for a more thorough evaluation of these issues and the development of a more robust and coherent solution.

CA-15-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — leave §10.1 at 5 dims; content quality + accessibility live in tooling only.
CA-15-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Adding more dimensions adds complexity without clear benefit. Content quality and accessibility checks are better handled in tooling.

CA-15-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: Reject — both should feed §7.6 with same coefficients as Phase A/B findings.
CA-15-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Content quality and accessibility are important aspects of product quality and should be reflected in the §7.6 score.

CA-15-A-v2-Q3.rationale: If the dimensions are important, they should always be enabled. The opt-in adds unnecessary complexity.

CA-15-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject the optional field too — no purpose information lives in ProductSSOT.
CA-15-B-v2-Q1.rationale: Purpose information is too subjective and unreliable to be stored in ProductSSOT. It's better to keep ProductSSOT focused on objective data.

CA-15-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: Defer to tooling — operator may run an inference helper script manually.
CA-15-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Inferred purpose can be useful, but it should be generated and reviewed manually, not automatically captured and stored.

CA-15-B-v2-Q3.pick_text: Reject — placeholder detection MUST be canonical to prevent placeholder text reaching production.
CA-15-B-v2-Q3.rationale: Placeholder detection is critical for preventing placeholder text from reaching production and should be a canonical rule.

CA-15-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — LLM-judged check is the heart of "Purpose-Driven" Optimization.
CA-15-C-v2-Q1.rationale: Without an LLM-judged check, the optimization loop loses its purpose-driven aspect. The LLM check is essential for ensuring that the product aligns with its intended purpose.

CA-15-C-v2-Q2.pick_text: Reject — replace with operator-supplied target string + LLM verifier.
CA-15-C-v2-Q2.rationale: An operator-supplied target string combined with an LLM verifier would provide a more reliable and flexible way to assess purpose fulfillment.

CA-15-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Reject — drift should never block; reduce to single advisory annotation.
CA-15-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Drift should be an advisory annotation only, as blocking the loop can lead to deadlock and prevent necessary updates.

CA-15-D-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — §27 should stay a hard blocking gate as v1 proposed.
CA-15-D-v2-Q1.rationale: The SSOT-Conformance Gate is critical for ensuring the quality and reliability of the system and should remain a hard blocking gate.

CA-15-D-v2-Q2.pick_text: Reject — every CA promotion should invalidate prior sign-offs as v1 proposed.
CA-15-D-v2-Q2.rationale: Every CA promotion should invalidate prior sign-offs to ensure that the system is always up-to-date and consistent.

perReviewer.overallNotes: This proposal introduces several changes that weaken critical aspects of the system and add unnecessary complexity. A more thorough evaluation is needed to develop a more robust and coherent solution.

objections.title: §10.1 dimension overlap
objections.detail: The proposed Content Quality dimension overlaps with existing UI/UX scoring criteria without clear differentiation boundaries. This creates ambiguity in §10.1 audit reports where the same visual/text issues could be counted under both dimensions, leading to inconsistent weighting and potential double-reporting.

objections.title: Optional purpose field risk
objections.detail: The free-form product_purpose field lacks validation or structured schema, making it vulnerable to misuse and misinterpretation. Without mandatory format rules or automated consistency checks, operators could enter contradictory, outdated, or overly vague purpose statements that undermine drift detection mechanisms.

objections.title: Drift thresholds arbitrary
objections.detail: The 20%/50% token-change thresholds for minor/major/critical drift annotations lack empirical justification. These arbitrary cutoffs may misclassify significant semantic changes as minor if token delta is low, or flag harmless refactors as critical drift, creating noise in governance records.

objections.title: Conformance scope maintenance
objections.detail: Maintaining CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md as the trigger for CEO re-sign introduces documentation drift risk. The file requires manual updates for every relevant CA, creating a brittle dependency where missed updates could invalidate sign-offs or allow non-conforming changes to bypass scrutiny.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: Enabling optional Content Quality dimension could flood telemetry with low-severity findings (e.g., grammar nitpicks) that distract from critical security/logic issues. Operators might disable all expanded dims to reduce noise, causing legitimate accessibility/content defects to reach production undetected.
adversarial.precedent: Google's Accelerated Mobile Pages (AMP) project initially treated validation errors as advisory, leading to compatibility breaks when developers ignored warnings. Similarly, advisory-only conformance gates here risk SSOT drift accumulation.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal adds operational complexity without proportional value: expanding audit dimensions creates scoring ambiguity, optional purpose fields invite inconsistency, and advisory conformance gates weaken governance rigor. Maintaining the status quo preserves scoring clarity while avoiding new failure modes in drift detection and sign-off protocols.

CA-15-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — leave §10.1 at 5 dims; content quality + accessibility live in tooling only.
CA-15-A-v2-Q1.rationale: Adding dimensions creates overlap with existing UI/UX scoring without clear problem-solving justification.

CA-15-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted: telemetry only; §7.6 formula UNCHANGED.
CA-15-A-v2-Q2.rationale: Preserves scoring integrity while allowing optional monitoring of non-critical dimensions.

CA-15-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted: expanded_quality_dims_enabled admin-only, default false.
CA-15-A-v2-Q3.rationale: Admin control appropriately restricts access to experimental/complex features.

CA-15-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (optional product_purpose field).
CA-15-B-v2-Q1.rationale: Avoids schema bloat while allowing operator context where beneficial.

CA-15-B-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (only described mode).
CA-15-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Eliminates hallucination risks from LLM-inferred purposes.

CA-15-B-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (placeholder detection in tooling, not canonical).
CA-15-B-v2-Q3.rationale: Placeholders are development artifacts, not runtime governance concerns.

CA-15-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (5 numeric exits; no LLM check).
CA-15-C-v2-Q1.rationale: Removes unreliable LLM judgments while maintaining quantifiable exit criteria.

CA-15-C-v2-Q2.rationale: Eliminates arbitrary magic numbers without replacement.

CA-15-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minor: log; major: operator dispose; critical: freeze fixes + Panel notify).
CA-15-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Tiered approach balances automation with human oversight.

CA-15-D-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify advisory framing BUT with admin dashboard prominence requirement.
CA-15-D-v2-Q1.rationale: Advisory with enforced visibility maintains flexibility while ensuring accountability.

CA-15-D-v2-Q2.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (scoped to CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md).
CA-15-D-v2-Q2.rationale: Scoping prevents unnecessary re-sign burden while covering critical changes.

perReviewer.overallNotes: v2 improves on v1 but retains residual complexity in dimension expansion that warrants monitoring.

objections.title: Telemetry-only weakens enforcement
objections.detail: CA-15-A-v2-Q2 moves content_quality and accessibility findings out of §7.6 entirely and into dashboard-only telemetry. That means a product can repeatedly fail copy/accessibility checks while still posting a clean readiness score, which undermines the existing score as an operator-facing risk signal.

objections.title: Admin-opt-in hides regressions
objections.detail: In CA-15-A-v2-Q3, dims 6 and 7 are off by default and admin-only, but the proposal still exposes them as quality dimensions in §10.1. This creates a split-brain audit where most products never see these checks in the acceptance path, so regressions can ship unless someone remembers to enable the knob product-by-product.

objections.title: Purpose field is too underspecified
objections.detail: CA-15-B-v2 replaces the canonical `purpose_record` with an optional free-form `product_purpose` string on `product_registry`, but provides no schema, length limit, provenance, or write-atomicity rule beyond a general note. That invites stale, contradictory, or promotional purpose text to become de facto canonical state without any structured validation or lifecycle management.

objections.title: Drift annotations may mask deadlocks
objections.detail: CA-15-C-v2-Q3 converts PURPOSE_DRIFT into minor/major/critical annotations, but the proposal does not specify a deterministic transition rule from annotation to operator disposition or freeze. In practice, major drift can accumulate across runs while still allowing the loop to continue, making the issue visible but not actionable.

objections.title: Scoped re-sign is gameable
objections.detail: CA-15-D-v2-Q2 limits CEO re-sign invalidation to files listed in `docs/governance/CONFORMANCE_SCOPE.md`. Because that scope file is itself editable documentation, the system can drift into a state where consequential governance changes are made adjacent to, but not inside, the tracked scope and therefore avoid re-sign requirements.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: A product with severe accessibility regressions and misleading purpose text can still pass the numeric readiness gate because the new findings are telemetry-only and the purpose field is optional. Compared with the status quo, that makes the system more likely to ship polished-looking but noncompliant products because the scoring surface no longer forces remediation.
adversarial.precedent: GitHub and other large platforms have repeatedly had accessibility regressions ship when checks were advisory rather than gating; similarly, optional metadata fields in product registries commonly rot into stale documentation unless enforced by schema and write-time validation. no precedent known for this exact combined design.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The strongest case for rejecting or deferring CA-15-v2 is that it decomposes a hard governance problem into advisory signals without providing compensating enforcement. Removing canonical purpose structure, making critical quality dimensions optional, and downgrading the SSOT conformance gate all reduce false positives, but they also shift responsibility to humans and dashboards in places where the platform previously had explicit invariants. If the goal is canonical integrity rather than monitoring, this rewrite may be too permissive to justify promotion.

CA-15-A-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — leave §10.1 at 5 dims; content quality + accessibility live in tooling only.
CA-15-A-v2-Q1.rationale: The proposal still lacks a strong enforcement path for dims 6 and 7, so keeping the canonical rubric at 5 dims avoids creating a quasi-canonical check that is easy to ignore. Tooling-only placement is cleaner until the governance path for these dimensions is specified.

CA-15-A-v2-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-15-A-v2-Q2.rationale: None of the options adequately addresses the enforcement problem created by making the new findings telemetry-only. If they are important enough to add, they should have a defined blocking or at least severity-sensitive path.

CA-15-A-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted: expanded_quality_dims_enabled admin-only, default false.
CA-15-A-v2-Q3.rationale: If the dimensions are retained at all, admin-only opt-in is the least risky way to limit blast radius. It at least prevents silent behavior changes for existing products.

CA-15-B-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject the optional field too — no purpose information lives in ProductSSOT.
CA-15-B-v2-Q1.rationale: An optional free-form purpose field is too weak to serve as reliable canonical state and too easy to rot. If purpose is important, it needs a structured, validated home rather than a nullable note field.

CA-15-B-v2-Q2.rationale: Dropping inferred and synthesized modes avoids hallucinated purpose becoming canonical state. Operator-supplied text is the only defensible source for such a sensitive field.

CA-15-B-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (placeholder detection in tooling, not canonical).
CA-15-B-v2-Q3.rationale: Placeholder detection belongs in linting or CI because it is heuristic and highly prone to false positives. Keeping it out of canonical SSOT avoids overfitting governance to brittle text-pattern rules.

CA-15-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — LLM-judged check is the heart of "Purpose-Driven" Optimization.
CA-15-C-v2-Q1.rationale: A purely numeric exit condition does not actually measure purpose alignment, which is the distinct claim of this workflow. Without an explicit purpose check, the loop becomes ordinary score chasing with renamed semantics.

CA-15-C-v2-Q2.rationale: A hardcoded 0.7 threshold is arbitrary and hard to defend as canonical. If the alignment check is removed, the threshold should go with it rather than lingering as a pseudo-policy knob.

CA-15-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minor: log; major: operator dispose; critical: freeze fixes + Panel notify).
CA-15-C-v2-Q3.rationale: Tiering drift is preferable to a single deadlock-prone gate because it preserves progress while escalating only severe cases. The freeze-for-critical path gives at least one hard stop where the risk is highest.

CA-15-D-v2-Q1.pick_text: Reject — §27 should stay a hard blocking gate as v1 proposed.
CA-15-D-v2-Q1.rationale: An advisory conformance gate is too weak for a canonical SSOT rule, because the whole point of conformance is to prevent divergence, not merely report it. If the gate cannot block, it will eventually be overridden in the cases that matter most.

CA-15-D-v2-Q2.pick_text: REJECT — none of the listed options is acceptable as specified
CA-15-D-v2-Q2.rationale: The scope-based invalidation rule is too easy to game and too dependent on a maintained file that itself may lag reality. A sound policy needs a more explicit, machine-enforced dependency model than the options provide.

perReviewer.overallNotes: The rewrite is cleaner than v1, but it still trades enforcement for observability in several places. That makes it safer operationally, yet weaker as canonical governance.

objections.title: Overly Complex §10.1 Extension
objections.detail: The proposal extends §10.1 with two new dimensions (Content Quality and Accessibility) but introduces complexity with admin-opt-in and telemetry-only findings. This may lead to inconsistent application and confusion among operators.

objections.title: Lack of Validation for `product_purpose`
objections.detail: The optional `product_purpose` field is introduced without a strict schema or validation rules, potentially leading to inconsistent or malformed data entry.

objections.title: Removal of `purpose_record` Block
objections.detail: Removing `purpose_record` as a canonical block may reduce the system's ability to track and validate product purpose, potentially impacting Purpose-Driven Optimization.

adversarial.worse_than_status_quo: If the optional `product_purpose` field is not properly validated or maintained, it could lead to incorrect or missing purpose information, potentially causing the system to produce suboptimal or irrelevant outputs.
adversarial.precedent: Similar design issues were seen in the 'API Documentation Project' where optional fields without strict validation led to data inconsistencies and downstream processing errors.

perReviewer.rejection_steelman: The proposal's structural changes, while addressing some Panel objections, introduce new complexities and potential risks, such as inconsistent application of the extended §10.1 dimensions and lack of validation for `product_purpose`. These changes may not be justified given the potential downsides.

CA-15-A-v2-Q1.rationale: The extension of §10.1 with admin-opt-in for new dimensions seems a reasonable compromise between adding new functionality and maintaining simplicity.

CA-15-B-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (placeholder detection in tooling, not canonical).

CA-15-C-v2-Q1.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (5 numeric exits; no LLM check).
CA-15-C-v2-Q1.rationale: The numeric exit criteria provide a clear and objective measure for loop exit, avoiding the potential unreliability of LLM-judged purpose-alignment checks.

CA-15-C-v2-Q2.rationale: Removing the hardcoded threshold eliminates a potential source of rigidity and allows for more flexible exit criteria.

CA-15-C-v2-Q3.pick_text: Ratify v2 as drafted (minor: log; major: operator dispose; critical: freeze fixes + Panel notify).
CA-15-C-v2-Q3.rationale: The tiered annotation for drift provides a nuanced approach to handling purpose drift, allowing for appropriate action based on severity.
